text.tspan: A Date is one number. Everything else (the year, the string, the time zone) is presentation.
A Date is a single number:
The one idea to hold on to
The stored number never has a time zone.
A zone appears only when you ASK for a
human-readable part, and it is whatever
zone the machine reading it is set to.
So the same Date shows a different hour in
London and in New York, and that is correct.
Formatting for people: use Intl, not string surgery
handle currency and "3 days ago" the same way.
Store and send UTC, an ISO string or a number; convert to local only at the moment you display. Months are ZERO-based
(0 is January) though days of the month are not. Date has no date-only type and no proper zone support, which is why the
Temporal API is on the way; until then, reach for a library for anything beyond simple formatting.
